name: hematologic cancer drugs overview
title: Drugs for blood cancers: classic cytotoxic classes (alkylating agents, antimetabolites, topoisomerase inhibitors, antimicrotubule agents) hit every dividing cell and each has an organ toxicity to watch; targeted and immune therapies (monoclonal antibodies and CAR-T cells, small molecules, checkpoint inhibitors) are matched to one molecule on the tumour

root.title: Systemic therapy for a blood cancer: hit EVERY dividing cell, or ONE target on the tumour?
lines: surgery only DIAGNOSES (resect a node) · radiation treats locally: see the RADIATION ONCOLOGY chart
glucocorticoids (prednisone, dexamethasone) kill lymphoid cells: lymphomas, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), acute B-cell leukemia, myeloma · also shrink swelling around metastases

groups.title: CLASSIC cytotoxic: every dividing cell
lines: every one: myelosuppression (infection), hair loss, mucositis

groups.title: TARGETED and IMMUNE: one molecule
lines: chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells: the patient's own, modified → relapsed acute lymphoblastic leukemia (< 26 y), relapsed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

head: h
Alkylating agents
cyclophosphamide, chlorambucil, cisplatin, carboplatin
how: DNA strands cannot separate → arrest → apoptosis

head: h
Antimetabolites
methotrexate, 5-fluorouracil, 6-mercaptopurine, 6-thioguanine
how: DNA and RNA cannot be made

head: h
Topoisomerase inhibitors
doxorubicin, daunorubicin, bleomycin (antitumour antibiotics) · etoposide
how: DNA cannot uncoil or stays broken → apoptosis

head: h
Monoclonal antibodies
how: CHECKPOINT: block programmed death-1 (PD-1) or its ligand PD-L1
pembrolizumab, nivolumab release the T-cell brakes: myeloma, Hodgkin, lung cancer

head: h
Small molecules
matched to one lesion
how: • imatinib: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase · ibrutinib: Bruton kinase
• all-trans retinoic acid: see the LEUKEMIA chart
